title: VIA Rail heading back to Quebec’s Gaspé region after 15 years — a partial win that brings hope
summary: Gaspé residents who have been waiting for the return of passenger train service since 2011 hope new federal investments and commitments from VIA Rail will lead to full service resumption down the…

image.caption: Eileen Jessop said that as a young adult, she could walk to her local train station in Chandler, Que., and get off in downtown Montreal the next morning. (Julia Page/CBC)

blocks.text: Montreal·New

Gaspé residents who have been waiting for the return of passenger train service since 2011 hope new federal investments and commitments from VIA Rail will lead to full service resumption down the line.
VIA Rail route to New Carlisle, Que., expected to resume by spring 2028
After 15 years of lobbying for the return of passenger train service to the Gaspé region, residents are finally seeing light at the end of the tunnel.

VIA Rail confirms it will resume partial service along the Baie des Chaleurs, reaching New Carlisle, Que., by spring 2028. This commitment from the Crown corporation paired with a $1.2 billion investment over three years for VIA Rail are fuelling hope full service to the Gaspé region — including the city that bears the same name — could return after a 15-year absence.
But the Quebec government needs to jump on board.

"It's great news in itself," said Éric Dubé, mayor of New Richmond and president of Société du chemin de fer de la Gaspésie (SCFG), a local non-profit organization in charge of repairing and operating the tracks.
The last passenger train reached the city of Gaspé in December 2011, after the tracks were deemed unsafe. In 2013, the final stop became Matapédia, leaving a 325-kilometre stretch without service.
For residents, news of the partial return of passenger train service brings back memories of an era when travelling to and from the Gaspé region was much more accessible.
"Back in the good years of the 1990s, as many as 28,000 passengers a year would take the train to the Gaspé Peninsula — so we’d love to be able to see that happen again someday," said Dubé.
The return of passenger train service to New Carlisle will cut the driving distance in half for travellers headed to Gaspé. (Lorena Suárez del Real/CBC)
The province, which has owned the tracks since 2015, has invested $350 million so far, which enabled the partial return of freight trains to the region.
Until now, VIA Rail was steadfast in its position to only bring back service to the region if the full line was refurbished, said Dubé.
"Before it was [all the way to the city of] Gaspé or nothing. Now they are agreeing to a partial return to New Carlisle, but with the objective the tracks be refurbished all the way to Gaspé."
The final stop for shipping goods is currently near the cement plant in Port-Daniel-Gascons.
VIA Rail’s partial return to Quebec’s Gaspé region — after 15 years — sparks hope

VIA Rail confirmed to CBC by e-mail the service between Quebec City and New Carlisle would run two to three times a week in a "phased return of service," while "working with the government of Quebec, infrastructure owners, local communities and all partners involved to move this important project forward."
Rail crucial for access to health care, local businesses

Dubé hopes the next provincial budget will include money to repair the last section of tracks between Port-Daniel-Gascons and Gaspé. That is also an ongoing demand from the local citizens' committee that has been at the forefront of the battle to bring back the train.
Residents on the Gaspé peninsula have been campaigning for the return of passenger train service since VIA Rail cut back service in 2011. (Julia Page/CBC)
"It's really disappointing to see how much the service has degraded in my lifetime," said Eileen Jessop, with the Coalition pour le retour des services d'un train de passagers en Gaspésie.

Jessop said going to see a show or visit family in Montreal used to be as simple as walking to the station in Chandler to board a night train. Now travelling back and forth to Matapedia adds on hours of driving.
"It's rough on the roads, it's rough on our vehicles, it's rough on our mental health."

items: Canada's 'Railway City' wants passenger trains back. Like in much of the country, it's not so simple

blocks.text: Many people who live in the region, including seniors, don't have access to a car, said Jessop, and often need to travel to Quebec City or Montreal to see medical specialists. The coalition also wants the province and VIA rail to arrange for more comfortable wagons designed for health care transportation.
Quebec’s new Transport Minister Nicolas Girard said there were no new developments for the moment, but his office said "an update could be made further down the line."

After numerous announcements from the province over the years to finalize repairs on the tracks, the project was sent back to the 'planning stage' in Quebec's 2025 infrastructure plan. (Julia Page/CBC)
Meanwhile, the Ministry of Transport "continues to work with VIA Rail with the aim of a resumption of passenger service," Girard's office said in a statement.
For Jessop, if rail service comes back, she wants to tick travelling from Gaspé to Vancouver off her bucket list.
"If the train comes back that's going to be one of my first things — taking the Canadian to the other side."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Julia Page is a radio and online journalist with CBC News, based in Quebec City. Her role is to travel to communities across the province, from Gaspé to Trois-Rivières to Rouyn-Noranda, to meet with Quebecers and reflect the issues affecting their communities.
